claim: Acetylcholine (ACh) is the most broadly used neurotransmitter in the C. elegans nervous system.
source: We systematically map here all cholinergic neuron types in the male and hermaphrodite C. elegans nervous system. We find that acetylcholine (ACh) is the most broadly used neurotransmitter
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing that 52 out of 118 neuron classes (159 out of 302 neurons) in the hermaphrodite are cholinergic, which is more than any other neurotransmitter system.

claim: Out of the 118 anatomically distinct neuron classes in the hermaphrodite, six classes (26 neurons) are GABAergic.
source: Specifically, out of the 118 anatomically distinct neuron classes in the hermaphrodite (amounting to a total of 302 neurons), six classes (26 neurons) are GABAergic (McIntire et al., 1993)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McIntire et al., 1993.

claim: 38 neuron classes (78 neurons) in the hermaphrodite are glutamatergic.
source: 38 are glutamatergic (78 neurons) (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: 13 neuron classes (26 neurons) in the hermaphrodite are aminergic.
source: 13 (26 neurons) are aminergic (i.e. serotonergic, dopaminergic, etc.; Chase and Koelle, 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chase and Koelle, 2007.

claim: Antibody staining against the vesicular acetylcholine (ACh) transporter, VAChT (encoded by unc-17) and the ACh-synthesizing choline acetyltransferase ChAT (encoded by cha-1) revealed the cholinergic identity of a number of neurons in the nervous system.
source: Antibody staining against the vesicular acetylcholine (ACh) transporter, VAChT (encoded by unc-17) and the ACh-synthesizing choline acetyltransferase ChAT (encoded by cha-1) revealed the cholinergic identity of a number of neurons in the nervous system (Alfonso et al., 1993; Duerr et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Alfonso et al., 1993 and Duerr et al., 2008.

claim: Due to the synaptic localization of the VAChT and ChAT proteins, expression could only be unambiguously assigned to about one dozen neuron classes.
source: However, due to the synaptic localization of the VAChT and ChAT proteins, expression could only be unambiguously assigned to about one dozen neuron classes, mostly in the ventral nerve cord and a few isolated head and tail neurons
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of previous antibody staining methods, based on the authors' interpretation of prior work.

claim: ACh is used by more than half of all neurons in the C. elegans nervous system.
source: We show that ACh is the most broadly used neurotransmitter in the C. elegans nervous system, employed by more than half of all neurons.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing that 159 out of 302 neurons in the hermaphrodite are cholinergic, which is more than half.

claim: unc-17/VAChT expression defines cholinergic identity and is present in 52 of the 118 classes of adult hermaphroditic neurons, amounting to 159 out of 302 neurons.
source: unc-17/VAChT expression defines cholinergic identity and is present in 52 of the 118 classes of adult hermaphroditic neurons, amounting to 159 out of 302 neurons (Figure 1, Figure 2A; Table 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in figures and tables showing unc-17 expression patterns.

claim: 85% (100/118) of all neuron classes are innervated by a cholinergic neuron.
source: The abundance of ACh usage is illustrated in an even more striking manner if one considers the C. elegans connectome (White et al., 1986): 85% (100/118) of all neuron classes are innervated by a cholinergic neuron (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 3 and the connectome data from White et al., 1986.

claim: All but one neuron class in the C. elegans nervous system are either cholinergic, receive cholinergic input or innervate a cholinergic neuron.
source: In other words, all but one neuron class in the C. elegans nervous system are either cholinergic, receive cholinergic input or innervate a cholinergic neuron.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of the connectome data presented in Table 3.

claim: The CAN neurons are the exception that do not receive cholinergic input and are not cholinergic themselves.
source: With one exception (the highly unusual CAN neurons, which show very little synaptic connectivity with any other neuron), all neurons that do not receive cholinergic input are either themselves cholinergic neurons or innervate neurons that are cholinergic (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 3 showing the connectivity patterns of neurons.

claim: cho-1/ChT expression extensively correlates with expression of unc-17/VAChT in the mature nervous system.
source: cho-1/ChT expression extensively correlates with expression of unc-17/VAChT, both in terms of onset (by threefold stage; data not shown) and cellular specificity in the mature nervous system.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of fosmid reporter expression patterns.

claim: In the hermaphrodite worm, all neurons that express cho-1 also express unc-17/VAChT.
source: In the hermaphrodite worm, all neurons that express cho-1 also express unc-17/VAChT (even though expression of unc-17 may be very low in at least one class, RIB)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of fosmid reporter expression patterns.

claim: 11 out of the 52 unc-17(+) classes do not express cho-1.
source: while 11 out of the 52 unc-17(+) classes do not express cho-1 (half of these neuron classes are in the pharyngeal nervous system; Figure 1;Table 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in figures and tables showing expression patterns.

claim: Expression of the acetylcholinesterase (AChE)-encoding ace genes does not correlate with unc-17 expression.
source: In contrast, as a previous analysis of small reporter gene fusions already suggested (Combes et al., 2003), expression of the acetylcholinesterase (AChE)-encoding ace genes does not correlate with unc-17 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' observations and a citation to Combes et al., 2003.

claim: Only one third of all cholinergic neuron classes express an ace gene.
source: First, only one third of all cholinergic neuron classes express an ace gene (Table 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: ace gene expression is observed in body wall muscle as well as in a few non-cholinergic neurons.
source: and second, expression is observed in body wall muscle as well as in a few non-cholinergic neurons (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1H.

claim: There are no overlaps in usage of the main neurotransmitter systems glutamate, GABA and ACh in the core nervous system of the hermaphrodite.
source: There are no overlaps in usage of the main neurotransmitter systems glutamate, GABA and ACh in the core nervous system of the hermaphrodite
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of neurotransmitter marker expression.

claim: Within the pharynx, one single neuron, the motor neuron M5, strongly expresses both cholinergic pathway genes unc-17 and cho-1 and, albeit very weakly, the glutamatergic marker eat-4/VGLUT.
source: but even in C. elegans, let alone other organisms, there have so far been only limited efforts to precisely map neurotransmitter identities on a system-wide level with single-neuron resolution. In C. elegans, a combination of direct staining methods and expression analysis of neurotransmitter-specific enzymes and transporters have defined the probably complete complement of GABAergic, glutamatergic and aminergic neurotransmitter systems. Specifically, out of the 118 anatomically distinct neuron classes in the hermaphrodite (amounting to a total of 302 neurons), six classes (26 neurons) are GABAergic (McIntire et al., 1993), 38 are glutamatergic (78 neurons) (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013) and 13 (26 neurons) are aminergic (i.e. serotonergic, dopaminergic, etc.; Chase and Koelle, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ADF, HSN, RIH and VC4/5 neurons are cholinergic, but also serotonergic.
source: There are, however, some overlaps of cholinergic identity with aminergic identity in the core nervous system: the ADF, HSN, RIH and VC4/5 neurons are cholinergic, but also serotonergic (Duerr et al., 2001; Sze et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Duerr et al., 2001 and Sze et al., 2000.

claim: All six VC neurons express unc-17/VAChT and are therefore cholinergic.
source: All six VC neurons express unc-17/VAChT and are therefore cholinergic
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of unc-17 expression.

claim: VC4 and VC5 are also serotonergic.
source: but VC4 and VC5 are also serotonergic (Duerr et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duerr et al., 1999.

claim: The expression of serotonergic identity in VC4 and VC5 correlates with a failure to express cho-1/ChT.
source: Notably, the expression of serotonergic identity in VC4 and VC5 correlates with a failure to express cho-1/ChT, which is only expressed in VC1,2,3 and VC6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5C.

claim: ACh is used by sensory neurons, interneurons and motor neurons.
source: ACh is used by sensory neurons, interneurons and motor neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' classification of cholinergic neurons.

claim: Of the 45 extrapharyngeal cholinergic neuron classes, 9 are sensory neurons, 19 are interneurons and 17 are motor neurons.
source: Of the 45 extrapharyngeal cholinergic neuron classes, 9 are sensory neurons, 19 are interneurons and 17 are motor neurons (Figure 2A; Table 2
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Table 2.

claim: Motor neurons have a preference for employing ACh (17/24 extrapharyngeal motor neuron classes are cholinergic).
source: Compared to other transmitter systems, motor neurons have a preference for employing ACh (17/24 extrapharyngeal motor neuron classes are cholinergic; Figure 2A; Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Table 2.

claim: Sensory neurons are predominantly glutamatergic (22/38 use Glu).
source: In contrast, sensory neurons are predominantly glutamatergic (22/38 use Glu)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter usage in sensory neurons.

claim: There is an appreciable number of cholinergic sensory neurons (9/38 extrapharyngeal sensory neuron classes use ACh).
source: but there is nevertheless an appreciable number of cholinergic sensory neurons (9/38 extrapharyngeal sensory neuron classes use ACh; Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 2.

claim: Most cholinergic sensory neurons have very shallow processing depth.
source: Intriguingly, most cholinergic sensory neurons have very shallow processing depth, i.e. are closely connected to the motor system (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: Two cholinergic sensory neurons (IL2 and URA) directly synapse onto muscle.
source: Two (IL2 and URA) directly synapse onto muscle (i.e. are sensory-motor neurons)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: Four cholinergic sensory neurons (ALN, PLN, ADF and URB) synapse directly onto motor neurons.
source: another four (ALN, PLN, ADF and URB) synapse directly onto motor neurons
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: Two cholinergic sensory neurons (URX and AWB) synapse onto cholinergic command interneurons that innervate motor neurons.
source: while another two (URX and AWB) synapse onto cholinergic command interneurons that innervate motor neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: URX and AWB are the only cases in the entire C. elegans nervous system where a multi-neuron pathway from sensory, via inter- to motor neurons is entirely made of exclusively one neurotransmitter system.
source: The latter two cases are the only cases in the entire C. elegans nervous system where a multi-neuron pathway from sensory, via inter- to motor neurons is entirely made of exclusively one neurotransmitter system.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: Glutamatergic sensory neurons do not display such a narrow processing depth as cholinergic sensory neurons.
source: In comparison, glutamatergic sensory neurons do not display such a narrow processing depth (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: ACh is the most broadly used neurotransmitter of interneurons (19 classes).
source: ACh is also the most broadly used neurotransmitter of interneurons (19 classes; compared to 11 glutamatergic; Figure 2A; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Table 1.

claim: GABA is only very sparsely used by interneurons (presently only 1 class).
source: In comparison to ACh and glutamate (Glu), the neurotransmitter GABA is only very sparsely used by interneurons (presently only 1 class; [McIntire et al., 1993])
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McIntire et al., 1993.

claim: Both ACh and Glu can act as inhibitory neurotransmitter through the gating of postsynaptic chloride channels.
source: this is no reflection of a paucity of inhibitory neurotransmission in C. elegans since both ACh and Glu can act as inhibitory neurotransmitter through the gating of postsynaptic chloride channels (see below).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of neurotransmitter function and is elaborated on later in the manuscript.

claim: The command interneurons are well-characterized central integrators of information flow in the nervous system that directly synapse onto motor neurons.
source: The most notable set of interneurons to which we assigned a cholinergic neurotransmitter identity are the command interneurons, which are well-characterized central integrators of information flow in the nervous system that directly synapse onto motor neurons (Chalfie et al., 1985; Von Stetina et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chalfie et al., 1985 and Von Stetina et al., 2006.

claim: The command interneurons AVA, AVE, AVD and PVC express the glutamate receptors glr-1 and nmr-1.
source: Expression of the cho-1 fosmid reporter overlapped with expression of the glutamate receptors glr-1 and nmr-1 in the AVA, AVE, AVD and PVC command interneurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The AVB command interneuron expresses sra-11 and acr-15.
source: To confirm the cholinergic identity of the AVB command interneuron, we crossed the cho-1 fosmid reporter with sra-11 and acr-15 reporters. Overlap of cho-1 with these two reporters allowed us to confirm that AVB expresses cholinergic identity genes.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: All command interneurons showed expression of the unc-17 fosmid reporter.
source: All command interneurons showed expression of the unc-17 fosmid reporter.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The adoption of cholinergic neurotransmitter identity does not correlate with position of the neuron within the nervous system, with the notable exception of cholinergic motor neurons in the ventral head ganglion and along the ventral nerve cord.
source: We find that the adoption of cholinergic neurotransmitter identity does not correlate with position of the neuron within the nervous system, as shown in Figure 2C, with the notable exception of cholinergic motor neurons in the ventral head ganglion and along the ventral nerve cord.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2C.

claim: There is no correlation between the adoption of cholinergic identity and developmental history of the neurons.
source: There is no correlation between the adoption of cholinergic identity and developmental history of the neurons. We arrived at this conclusion by mapping neurotransmitter identity onto the entire lineage diagram and not detecting any obvious lineage clusters of cells that uniquely employ ACh (or any other neurotransmitter; Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: A neurotransmitter identity can now be assigned to ~90% of all neuron classes (102/118) and total neurons (275/302).
source: With the identification of the complete set of cholinergic neurons, and with the consideration of previously identified glutamatergic, GABAergic and monoaminergic neurons, a neurotransmitter identity can now be assigned to ~90% of all neuron classes (102/118) and total neurons (275/302; Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 2.

claim: About half of the remaining 16 'orphan' neuron classes display a notable paucity or even absence of synaptic vesicles and/or are predominated by dark staining vesicles.
source: While some of the remaining orphan neurons (e.g. the prominent olfactory neuron AWA) contain small synaptic vesicles that are indicative of the usage of an as yet uncharacterized neurotransmitter system, about half of the remaining 16 'orphan' neuron classes display, according to John White's EM analysis, a notable paucity or even absence of synaptic vesicles and/or are predominated by dark staining vesicles (e.g. AVF, AVH, AVJ, RIP) (White et al., 1986)
evidence: This claim is based on EM analysis from White et al., 1986.

claim: Orphan neurons with a paucity of synaptic vesicles either signal mostly via electrical synapses or via neuropeptides.
source: suggesting that these neurons either signal mostly via electrical synapses or via neuropeptides.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation of vesicle paucity.

claim: The circuitry associated with the motor neurons of the ventral nerve cord is mainly cholinergic (with the exception of the GABAergic DD/VD motor neurons).
source: the circuitry associated with the motor neurons of the ventral nerve cord show the striking feature of being mainly cholinergic (with the exception of the GABAergic DD/VD motor neurons; Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3B.

claim: Most motor neurons (SAB, DA, DB, VA, VB, AS) employ ACh.
source: That is, not only do most motor neurons ('MNs')(SAB, DA, DB, VA, VB, AS) employ ACh
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity.

claim: All neurons that innervate the ventral nerve cord motor neurons are also cholinergic.
source: but all neurons that innervate these neurons (and that are also strongly interconnected among each other) are also cholinergic. This includes the command interneurons AVA, AVB, AVE, AVD, PVC, as well as the DVA interneuron, which is also closely associated with the motor circuit (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3B.

claim: The command interneurons AVA, AVB, AVE, AVD, PVC, and the DVA interneuron have been defined as a 'rich club' of neurons due to the extent of their interconnectedness.
source: Due to the extent of their interconnectedness, this group of six interneuron classes has previously been defined as a 'rich club' of neurons (Towlson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Towlson et al., 2013.

claim: Genetic silencing of the C. elegans nervous system, achieved through elimination of the snb-1/synaptobrevin gene, has no impact on the expression of cholinergic identity markers in arrested L1 larvae.
source: However, we find that genetic silencing of the C. elegans nervous system, achieved through elimination of the snb-1/synaptobrevin gene, has no impact on the expression of cholinergic identity markers in arrested L1 larvae (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Compared to other neurotransmitter systems (particularly Glu) ACh is enriched, but not exclusively located to lower levels of information processing.
source: Both types of representations quantify and effectively visualize what the identity of many of the cholinergic neurons already suggested: compared to other neurotransmitter systems (particularly Glu) ACh is enriched, but not exclusively located to lower levels of information processing.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of processing depth presented in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Five 3-neuron motifs and fourteen 4-neuron motifs are significantly enriched in the C. elegans connectome.
source: Using previously described approaches (Milo et al., 2002) (see Materials and methods), we identified five 3-neuron motifs and fourteen 4-neuron motifs that are significantly enriched in the C. elegans connectome using the latest connectivity dataset (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3E and uses methods from Milo et al., 2002.

claim: ACh was enriched at a specific position in 11 out of 19 enriched network motifs.
source: ACh was enriched at a specific position in 11 out of these 19 motifs.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs.

claim: There is a strong trend of ACh being more frequently used at the downstream end of the signaling flow within specific motifs, while Glu tends to be located at upstream positions within motifs.
source: Generally, there is a strong trend of ACh being more frequently used at the downstream end of the signaling flow within specific motifs, while Glu tends to be located at upstream positions within motifs (Figure 3E)
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: In the 'regulated mutual motif', each one of the interconnected neurons is enriched for a specific neurotransmitter.
source: In one 3-neuron motif, previously termed a 'regulated mutual motif' (Milo et al., 2004), each one of the interconnected neurons is enriched for a specific neurotransmitter
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs and cites Milo et al., 2004.

claim: 224 occurrences of the 'regulated mutual motif' can be found in the C. elegans hermaphroditic connectome.
source: 224 occurrences of this motif can be found in the C. elegans hermaphroditic connectome.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: The 'regulated mutual motif' is significantly enriched for the presence of cholinergic neurons in either position 2 or 3, or in both.
source: This motif is significantly enriched for the presence of cholinergic neurons in either position 2 or 3, or in both.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs.

claim: Position 1 of the 'regulated mutual motif' is significantly enriched for Glu usage.
source: Notably, position 1 is significantly enriched for Glu usage.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs.

claim: In 146 out of the 224 'regulated mutual motif' occurrences, ACh is used by both neuron '2' and '3'.
source: In 146 out of the 224 motif occurrences, ACh is used by both neuron '2' and '3' (listed in Table 4)
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 4.

claim: In the first type of 'regulated mutual motif', reciprocally connected command interneurons are either innervated by a sensory neuron or by an interneuron.
source: In the first type, reciprocally connected command interneurons are either innervated by a sensory neuron or by an interneuron (Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 4.

claim: In virtually all cases of the first type of 'regulated mutual motif', the innervating sensory neurons are glutamatergic.
source: In virtually all of these cases, the innervating sensory neurons are glutamatergic.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs.

claim: In many cases of the first type of 'regulated mutual motif', the reciprocally connected command interneurons are neurons that control different directions of movement (forward vs. reverse).
source: In many cases, the reciprocally connected command interneurons are neurons that control different directions of movement (forward vs. reverse; Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 4.

claim: In the second type of 'regulated mutual motif', the SMD or RMD head motor neurons are reciprocally connected and innervated again either by mostly glutamatergic sensory neurons or by interneurons.
source: In the second type, the SMD or RMD head motor neurons are reciprocally connected and innervated again either by mostly glutamatergic sensory neurons or by interneurons (Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 4.

claim: The C. elegans genome encodes not only conventional, excitatory ACh-gated cation channels, but also inhibitory ACh-gated anion channels.
source: The C. elegans genome encodes not only conventional, excitatory ACh-gated cation channels, but also inhibitory ACh-gated anion channels (Hobert, 2013; Putrenko et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hobert, 2013 and Putrenko et al., 2005.

claim: The C. elegans genome encodes at least four ACh-gated anion channels, acc-1 through acc-4.
source: The C. elegans genome encodes at least four ACh-gated anion channels, acc-1 through acc-4, two of which (acc-1 and acc-2) were electrophysiologically validated to be inhibitory receptors, while the function of two others (acc-3 and acc-4) is less clear (Putrenko et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Putrenko et al., 2005.

claim: acc-1 and acc-2 were electrophysiologically validated to be inhibitory receptors.
source: two of which (acc-1 and acc-2) were electrophysiologically validated to be inhibitory receptors, while the function of two others (acc-3 and acc-4) is less clear (Putrenko et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Putrenko et al., 2005.

claim: An acc-3 fosmid reporter showed no appreciable expression throughout the animal.
source: An acc-3 fosmid reporter showed no appreciable expression throughout the animal
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: acc-1 and acc-2 fosmid reporters show very restricted and non-overlapping expression in the adult nervous system.
source: whereas acc-1 and acc-2 fosmid reporters show very restricted and non-overlapping expression in the adult nervous system (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The acc-1 fosmid reporter is expressed in a subset of cholinergic neurons, including cholinergic neurons in the ventral nerve cord, the retrovesicular ganglion and a few head neurons.
source: The acc-1 fosmid reporter is expressed in a subset of cholinergic neurons, including cholinergic neurons in the ventral nerve cord, the retrovesicular ganglion and a few head neurons (including the SMD, RMD motor neurons, the AVA and AVE command interneurons and the SAA neurons).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: A small number of glutamatergic neurons also express acc-1.
source: A small number of glutamatergic neurons also express acc-1 (including the pharyngeal neurons MI and M3, the PLM neurons and an unidentified neuronal pair in the lateral ganglion).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The acc-2 fosmid reporter is expressed in a distinct, small set of glutamatergic neurons (RIA, RIG, PHA, AIZ) and cholinergic neurons (URX, RIH).
source: The acc-2 fosmid reporter is expressed in a distinct, small set of glutamatergic neurons (RIA, RIG, PHA, AIZ) and cholinergic neurons (URX, RIH).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The acc-2 fosmid reporter is strongly expressed in the newly identified male-specific MCM neurons.
source: We also found that the acc-2 fosmid reporter is strongly expressed in the newly identified male-specific MCM neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The acc-4 fosmid reporter is expressed almost exclusively in almost all of the 52 classes of cholinergic neurons.
source: The acc-4 fosmid reporter showed the most striking expression pattern. As assessed by coexpression with cho-1, the acc-4 fosmid reporter is expressed almost exclusively in almost all of the 52 classes of cholinergic neurons (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The only cholinergic neuron classes not expressing acc-4 are the ASJ and RIB neurons.
source: The only cholinergic neuron classes not expressing acc-4 are the ASJ and RIB neurons
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: The only acc-4-expressing non-cholinergic neurons are the AVF neurons.
source: and the only acc-4-expressing non-cholinergic neurons are the AVF neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: If acc-4 indeed is able to operate as inhibitory receptor, most cholinergic neurons can be silenced by presynaptically released ACh.
source: If acc-4 indeed is able to operate as inhibitory receptor (as suggested by its sequence), this expression data indicates that most cholinergic neurons can be silenced by presynaptically released ACh.
evidence: This is a conditional inference based on the expression pattern of acc-4 and its sequence similarity to inhibitory receptors.

claim: More than half of all cholinergic neurons are innervated by cholinergic neurons.
source: In line with this prediction, more than half of all cholinergic neurons are innervated by cholinergic neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: Laser ablation, electrophysiological and modeling data indicate that specific command interneuron classes inhibit each others activity.
source: This is particularly intriguing in light of laser ablation, electrophysiological and modeling data which indicate that specific command interneuron classes inhibit each others activity (Rakowski et al., 2013; Roberts et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rakowski et al., 2013 and Roberts et al., 2016.

claim: Regulated mutual motifs with negative interactions can operate as toggle switches that commit to one specific drive (forward movement) while inhibiting the alternative (reversal) drive.
source: Regulated mutual motifs with negative interactions can operate as toggle switches that commit to one specific drive (forward movement) while inhibiting the alternative (reversal) drive.
evidence: This is a general statement about the function of network motifs, based on established knowledge.

claim: A number of cholinergic neurons (including the command interneurons, but also VNC MNs) are also known to express excitatory ACh-gated ion channels (acr genes).
source: However, it is important to keep in mind that a number of cholinergic neurons (including the command interneurons, but also VNC MNs) are also known to express excitatory ACh-gated ion channels (acr genes; www.wormbase.org)
evidence: This claim is based on information from www.wormbase.org.

claim: A substantial number of cholinergic neurons that express acc-4 are not innervated by cholinergic neurons.
source: We furthermore note that a substantial number of cholinergic neurons that express acc-4 are not innervated by cholinergic neurons (as predicted by the connectome)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: ACC-4 may act as an inhibitory autoreceptor on cholinergic neurons.
source: raising the intriguing possibility that ACC-4 may act as an inhibitory autoreceptor on cholinergic neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the observation that some acc-4 expressing neurons are not innervated by other cholinergic neurons.

claim: In the context of gene expression networks, negative autoregulation can confer a number of useful functions, including speed-up of circuit responses and noise reduction.
source: In the context of gene expression networks, negative autoregulation can confer a number of useful functions, including speed-up of circuit responses and noise reduction (Hart and Alon, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hart and Alon, 2013.

claim: The C. elegans male contains 91 sex-specific neurons, defining 24 classes, most of them located in the tail.
source: The C. elegans male contains 91 sex-specific neurons, defining 24 classes, most of them located in the tail.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomy of the male nervous system.

claim: 16 out of 24 male-specific neuron classes are cholinergic.
source: We find that 16 out of these 24 classes are cholinergic (Figure 5A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Table 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and Table 5.

claim: The CEM sensory neurons are the only male-specific head neurons and are cholinergic.
source: These cholinergic neurons include the only male-specific head neurons (the CEM sensory neurons)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity in male-specific neurons.

claim: The CA neurons are an additional, male-specific class of motor neurons in the ventral nerve cord.
source: and an additional, male-specific class of motor neurons in the ventral nerve cord, the CA neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity in male-specific neurons.

claim: ACh is the most broadly used neurotransmitter in the male nervous system.
source: The three key themes observed in the hermaphrodite nervous system also apply to the male-specific neurons: (1) ACh is the most broadly used neurotransmitter in the male nervous system
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity in male-specific neurons.

claim: ACh is used in sensory, inter- and motor neurons of the male-specific nervous system.
source: (2) ACh is used in sensory, inter- and motor neurons of the male-specific nervous system
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity in male-specific neurons.

claim: The male-specific sensory neurons that are cholinergic are all in close proximity to the motor circuitry.
source: (3) the male-specific sensory neurons that are cholinergic are all in close proximity to the motor circuitry: most of them directly innervate muscle (i.e. are sensory/motor neurons; PCB, PCC, SPC; several ray neurons) while all others (HOB, SPV) innervate motor neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the connectome.

claim: The PVV neurons and the R6A neurons express unc-17/VAChT and eat-4/VGLUT.
source: Like in the pharyngeal nervous system, we found neurons labeled by two conventional fast transmitters markers– the PVV neurons and the R6A neurons express unc-17/VAChT and eat-4/VGLUT (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: ACh/Glu cotransmission has been observed in some central synapses in the vertebrate central nervous system.
source: ACh/Glu cotransmission has been observed in some central synapses in the vertebrate central nervous system (Nishimaru et al., 2005; Ren et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nishimaru et al., 2005 and Ren et al., 2011.

claim: The male-specific CEM neurons are generated in the embryo in both sexes, but are removed specifically in the hermaphrodite through programmed cell death.
source: The two pairs of CEM neurons are generated in the embryo in both sexes, but are removed specifically in the hermaphrodite through programmed cell death (Sulston et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: The CEM neurons only start expressing cholinergic identity features at the L4 larval stage.
source: We examined the onset of cholinergic differentiation of these neurons in males and found that they only start expressing cholinergic identity features at the L4 larval stage (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5A.

claim: The HSN and VC neurons are hermaphrodite-specific cholinergic neurons.
source: The same applies to the two classes of hermaphrodite-specific cholinergic neurons, the HSN and VC neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of neurotransmitter identity.

claim: HSN is born embryonically, and VCs are born in the first larval stage, yet onset of cholinergic pathway genes is only observed in late L4 larval stages.
source: HSN is born embryonically, and VCs are born in the first larval stage, yet onset of cholinergic pathway genes is only observed in late L4 larval stages (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5B-C.

claim: The onset of cholinergic marker expression in the VC neurons is observed in late L4 stage animals, contrasting the late L1 onset in the VA, VB and AS-type neurons.
source: In these neurons, the onset of cholinergic marker expression is observed already in late L1 stage animals, contrasting the late L4 onset in the VC neurons (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5C.

claim: The AIM neuron pair expresses cholinergic markers only in males, but not hermaphrodites.
source: We were therefore surprised to note a pair of neurons, located next to the cholinergic AIY interneurons in the ventral head ganglion that expressed cholinergic markers only in males, but not hermaphrodites (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5D.

claim: In hermaphrodites, the AIM neurons are glutamatergic, expressing the vesicular glutamate transporter eat-4/VGLUT.
source: In hermaphrodites, the AIM neurons are glutamatergic, expressing the vesicular glutamate transporter eat-4/VGLUT (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5D.

claim: In males, the AIM neurons also initially express eat-4/VGLUT, but only until the L3 stage.
source: In males, the AIM neurons also initially express eat-4/VGLUT, but only until the L3 stage.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' observations of reporter gene expression.

claim: During the L4 stage in males, eat-4/VGLUT expression becomes downregulated and unc-17/VAChT and cho-1/ChT expression becomes induced in AIM neurons.
source: During the L4 stage eat-4/VGLUT expression becomes downregulated and unc-17/VAChT and cho-1/ChT expression becomes induced (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5E.

claim: Masculinization of the AIM neurons in otherwise hermaphroditic animals results in downregulation of eat-4/VGLUT and upregulation of cho-1 expression.
source: We found that masculinization of the AIM neurons ('eat-4prom11::fem-3') in otherwise hermaphroditic animals results in downregulation of eat-4/VGLUT and upregulation of cho-1 expression (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5F.

claim: Feminization of AIM in male animals results in sustained eat-4 expression and no induction of cho-1 expression.
source: Conversely, feminization of AIM in male animals results in sustained eat-4 expression and no induction of cho-1 expression (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5F.

claim: The neurotransmitter switch in AIM neurons is programmed cell autonomously.
source: These results demonstrate that the neurotransmitter switch is programmed cell autonomously.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental results showing that cell-specific manipulation of sex determination genes affects neurotransmitter identity.

claim: The POU homeobox gene unc-86 controls the cholinergic identity of three cholinergic sensory neurons (IL2, URA, URB).
source: Specifically, we have reported that the POU homeobox gene unc-86 controls the cholinergic identity of three cholinergic sensory neurons (IL2, URA, URB) (Zhang et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: The LIM homeobox gene ttx-3 controls the cholinergic identity of two cholinergic interneurons (AIY, AIA).
source: that the LIM homeobox gene ttx-3 controls the cholinergic identity of two cholinergic interneurons (AIY, AIA) (Altun-Gultekin et al., 2001)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Altun-Gultekin et al., 2001.

claim: The COE (Collier/Olf/EBF)-type Zn-finger factor unc-3 controls cholinergic identity of most motor neuron classes in the VNC as well as the SAB head motor neurons.
source: and that the COE (Collier/Olf/EBF)-type Zn-finger factor unc-3 controls cholinergic identity of most motor neuron classes in the VNC as well as the SAB head motor neurons (Kratsios et al., 2011, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011 and 2015.

claim: A total of 7 regulators control the identity of 20 of the 52 cholinergic neuron types.
source: Our analysis resulted in the identification of a total of 7 regulators that control the identity of 20 of the 52 cholinergic neuron types (Table 6; Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 6 and Figure 6.

claim: There is a striking preponderance of homeodomain containing proteins in the transcription factors that regulate cholinergic identity.
source: In line with a similar observation that we made upon analysis of glutamatergic neuron identity control (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013), we observed a striking preponderance of homeodomain containing proteins in the transcription factors that we newly identified as cholinergic identity regulators.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the transcription factors identified and cites Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: The three LIM homeobox genes lim-4, lin-11 and ceh-14 control cholinergic identity of six distinct cholinergic neuron types.
source: Specifically, we found that the three LIM homeobox genes lim-4, lin-11 and ceh-14 control cholinergic identity of six distinct cholinergic neuron types, including sensory neurons (lim-4 in AWB), interneurons (lin-11 in PVP; ceh-14 in AIM, PVC) and motor neurons (ceh-14 in PVN, lim-4 in SMB; Table 6; Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 6 and Figure 6.

claim: lim-7, the C. elegans homolog of vertebrate Islet, is not required to specify cholinergic identity in C. elegans.
source: However, we find that lim-7, the C. elegans homolog of vertebrate Islet, which specifies cholinergic identity in the spinal cord and forebrain in mice (Cho et al., 2014), is not required to specify cholinergic identity in C. elegans (as assessed by normal cho-1 expression throughout the nervous system in lim-7 null mutants; data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations and cites Cho et al., 2014.

claim: The Pitx-type homeobox gene unc-30 controls cholinergic identity of the PVP interneurons (in conjunction with lin-11).
source: Moreover, we found that the Pitx-type homeobox gene unc-30 controls cholinergic identity of the PVP interneurons (in conjunction with lin-11)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: The POU homeobox gene unc-86 controls cholinergic identity of the URX, RIH and male-specific CEM neurons.
source: and that the POU homeobox gene unc-86 controls cholinergic identity of the URX, RIH and male-specific CEM neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: unc-86, in conjunction with ceh-14, is required for the AIM neurons to adopt their cholinergic identity in males.
source: unc-86, in conjunction with ceh-14, is also required for the AIM neurons to adopt their cholinergic identity in males
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: unc-86 and ceh-14 also control glutamatergic identity of the AIM neurons in hermaphrodites (and males till the third larval stage).
source: both factors also control glutamatergic identity of the AIM neurons in hermaphrodites (and males till the third larval stage; Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6.

claim: All of the transcription factors that control cholinergic identity are continuously expressed throughout the life of these neurons.
source: All of the above-mentioned transcription factors are continuously expressed throughout the life of these neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that these factors not only initiate but also maintain cholinergic identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: unc-42, a Prox-type homeobox gene, is a regulator of cholinergic gene expression in RMD motor neurons.
source: From a EMS-induced genetic mutant screen that we conducted for regulators of RMD neuron identity (see Materials and methods), we uncovered unc-42, a Prox-type homeobox gene as a regulator of cholinergic gene expression in RMD motor neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' genetic screen.

claim: unc-42 affects cholinergic identity of four additional, distinct types of cholinergic head neurons, most of them motor neurons.
source: We also found that unc-42 affects cholinergic identity of four additional, distinct types of cholinergic head neurons, most of them motor neurons (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6.

claim: unc-42 is continuously expressed in all the postmitotic neuron types it regulates.
source: unc-42 is continuously expressed in all these postmitotic neuron types (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: unc-3 regulates expression of the cholinergic identity genes cho-1 and unc-17 in all command interneurons.
source: In addition to the previously reported impact of unc-3 on cholinergic ventral cord motor neuron identity (SAB-, A-, B-, AS-type MNs), we found that unc-3 regulates expression of the cholinergic identity genes cho-1 and unc-17 in all command interneurons (Figure 7, Table 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7 and Table 6.

claim: The PDA, PDB, PVN and DVA tail neurons require unc-3 for their normal expression of cholinergic identity genes.
source: Moreover, the PDA, PDB, PVN and DVA tail neurons also require unc-3 for their normal expression of cholinergic identity genes (Figure 7, Table 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7 and Table 6.

claim: unc-3 is expressed in all the cholinergic neuron types it regulates, including the command interneurons.
source: Using a fosmid reporter and a gfp reporter inserted into the unc-3 locus through CRISPR-Cas9, we confirmed expression of unc-3 in all these cholinergic neuron types, including the command interneurons (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7A.

claim: Most of the transcriptional regulators that control cholinergic identity also control other identity features.
source: Most of the transcriptional regulators that we defined here control not only cholinergic identity in the respective neuron classes, but also control other identity features.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the effects of transcription factor mutations.

claim: Loss of unc-3 affects multiple aspects of PDA motor neuron identity (expression of the exp-1 ligand gated ion channel, ace-3/4 cholinesterase, cog-1 homeobox gene).
source: For example, we find that loss of unc-3 affects multiple aspects of PDA motor neuron identity (expression of the exp-1 ligand gated ion channel, ace-3/4 cholinesterase, cog-1 homeobox gene)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Loss of unc-42 affects metabotropic glutamate receptor (mgl-1) expression in the RMD neurons.
source: and loss of unc-42 affects metabotropic glutamate receptor (mgl-1) expression in the RMD neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Loss of ceh-14 affects neuropeptide (flp-10) expression, as well as the serotonergic co-transmitter identity of the AIM neurons and it affects expression of the ionotropic glutamate receptors nmr-1 and glr-1 in the PVC command interneuron.
source: Apart from affecting cholinergic identity, loss of ceh-14 affects neuropeptide (flp-10) expression, as well as the serotonergic co-transmitter identity of the AIM neurons and it affects expression of the ionotropic glutamate receptors nmr-1 and glr-1 in the PVC command interneuron (Figure 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 8.

claim: lin-11 and unc-30 control many terminal identity features of the PVP.
source: In addition, lin-11 and unc-30 were previously found to control many terminal identity features of the PVP (Hutter, 2003) and these two factors also control cholinergic identity of PVP (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hutter, 2003 and data presented in Figure 6E.

claim: lim-4 controls cholinergic identity of the AWB neurons but also several other identity features.
source: Similarly, lim-4 controls cholinergic identity of the AWB neurons but also several other identity features (Alqadah et al., 2015; Sagasti et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Alqadah et al., 2015 and Sagasti et al., 1999.

claim: The serotonergic identity of the hermaphrodite specific motor neurons HSN is controlled by the unc-86 POU homeobox gene.
source: The serotonergic identity of the hermaphrodite specific motor neurons HSN is controlled by the unc-86 POU homeobox gene (Sze et al., 2002)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sze et al., 2002.

claim: unc-86 does not affect unc-17/VAChT expression in HSN.
source: but unc-86 does not affect unc-17/VAChT expression in HSN (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: In all motor neurons in which unc-3 is expressed (SAB head motor neurons, A- B- and AS-type VNC MNs), unc-3 controls neurotransmitter identity and a multitude of other terminal molecular markers.
source: We had previously shown that in all motor neurons in which unc-3 is expressed (SAB head motor neurons, A- B- and AS-type VNC MNs), unc-3 not only controls neurotransmitter identity, but also a multitude of other terminal molecular markers (Kratsios et al., 2015, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2015 and 2011.

claim: The activity of unc-3 in the AVA, AVB, AVD, AVE and PVC command interneurons and DVA interneuron appears to be restricted to select subfeatures of these neurons.
source: In contrast, the activity of unc-3 in the AVA, AVB, AVD, AVE and PVC command interneurons and DVA interneuron appears to be restricted to select subfeatures of these neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of the effects of unc-3 mutations.

claim: Not a single identity marker besides the cholinergic reporter genes is affected in the command interneurons and DVA interneuron in worms lacking unc-3.
source: We arrived at this conclusion by analyzing the expression of more than ten additional identity markers of these unc-3-expressing neurons (including glutamate receptors, neuropeptides and ion channels). Not a single one besides the cholinergic reporter genes is affected in the worms lacking unc-3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1; Table 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Table 7.

claim: Within the command interneurons AVA, AVD and AVE, three transcription factors, unc-42 (homeobox), fax-1 (nuclear hormone receptor) and cfi-1 (ARID-type), control subsets of unc-3-independent terminal identity markers.
source: Within a subset of these neurons, namely the command interneurons AVA, AVD and AVE, three transcription factors, unc-42 (homeobox), fax-1 (nuclear hormone receptor) and cfi-1 (ARID-type), have been shown to control subsets of these unc-3-independent terminal identity markers (Table 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 8.

claim: unc-3 is expressed and required for the adoption of cholinergic identity in all neurons in the ventral nerve cord motor circuit.
source: Strikingly, unc-3 is expressed and required for the adoption of cholinergic identity in all neurons in this circuit (schematized in Figure 9A; data in Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 9A and Figure 7B.

claim: unc-3 is a circuit-associated transcription factor that is selectively associated with the ventral nerve cord motor circuit.
source: unc-3 is therefore a circuit-associated transcription factor that is selectively associated with this circuit (unc-3 is expressed only in a few neurons outside this circuit) and that defines a critical feature of the circuit, namely the ability of neurons in the circuit to communicate among each other.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of unc-3 expression and function.

claim: In unc-3 mutants, UNC-7::GFP puncta, which visualize electrical synapses, are severely reduced.
source: UNC-7::GFP puncta, visualized with a translational reporter are severely reduced in unc-3 mutants (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7C.

claim: Expression of a transcriptional, fosmid-based unc-7 reporter is unaffected in unc-3 mutants.
source: Expression of a transcriptional, fosmid-based unc-7 reporter is unaffected in unc-3 mutants (data not shown)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: unc-3 affects electrical synapse formation at a step independent of regulation of innexin expression.
source: leading us to conclude that unc-3 affects electrical synapse formation at a step independent of regulation of innexin expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that transcriptional unc-7 expression is unaffected but UNC-7::GFP puncta are reduced.

claim: In unc-3 null mutants, AVA receives less chemical synaptic input from within the motor circuit and it makes less chemical synapses onto other motor neurons and onto other command interneurons.
source: In unc-3 null mutants, we found connectivity defects on all levels: AVA receives less chemical synaptic input from within the motor circuit (i.e. from other command interneurons) and it makes less chemical synapses onto other motor neurons and onto other command interneurons (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7D.

claim: There is an overall disorganization of the placement of axonal processes in the VNC of unc-3 mutants.
source: There is also an overall disorganization of the placement of axonal processes in the VNC of unc-3 mutants (data not shown)
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: In unc-3 mutants, AVA still neighbors the command interneurons that it normally connects to, indicating that the connectivity defects are not a secondary consequence of placement defects.
source: however, AVA still neighbors the command interneurons that it normally connects to, indicating that the connectivity defects are not a secondary consequence of placement defects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that AVA is still adjacent to its normal synaptic partners despite connectivity defects.

claim: Non-cholinergic synaptic inputs from sensory neurons into the motor circuit appear not to be affected by unc-3.
source: Non-cholinergic synaptic inputs from sensory neurons into the motor circuit appear not to be affected by unc-3.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: The synaptic connection of the glutamatergic PHB neuron to the AVA interneuron is unaffected in unc-3 mutants.
source: We arrived at this conclusion by examining the synaptic connections of the glutamatergic PHB neuron to the AVA interneuron, normally made in the pre-anal ganglion (White et al., 1986). This synaptic connection can be visualized using a GFP reconstitution system ('GRASP'; (Park et al., 2011). We find these synaptic GFP signals to be unaffected in unc-3 mutants (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations using GRASP and cites White et al., 1986 and Park et al., 2011.

claim: The pan-circuit control of cholinergic neurotransmitter identity by unc-3 is mediated via a single UNC-3 binding site ('COE motif') controlling neurotransmitter pathway genes.
source: Remarkably, the pan-circuit control of cholinergic neurotransmitter identity by unc-3 is mediated via a single UNC-3 binding site ('COE motif') controlling neurotransmitter pathway genes.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Deletion of the COE motif in the context of the cho-1/ChT fosmid-based reporter eliminates expression not only in the ventral nerve cord motor neurons, but also in all other unc-3 dependent cholinergic neurons.
source: Its deletion in the context of the cho-1/ChT fosmid-based reporter eliminates expression not only in the ventral nerve cord motor neurons, but also in all other unc-3 dependent cholinergic neurons, not just within the motor neuron circuit, but also outside the circuit (Figure 10A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 10A-C.

claim: A 280 bp region from the cho-1 and a 250 bp region from the unc-17 locus that contain the COE motif are not sufficient to drive expression in all unc-3-dependent inter- and motor neurons of the motor circuit, but only drives expression in motor neurons.
source: On the other hand, a 280 bp region from the cho-1 and a 250 bp region from the unc-17 locus that contain the COE motif are not sufficient to drive expression in all unc-3-dependent inter- and motor neurons of the motor circuit, but only drives expression in motor neurons (Figure 10D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 10D and E.

claim: unc-3 may cooperate with distinct cofactors in distinct neuron types.
source: This finding suggests that unc-3 may cooperate with distinct cofactors in distinct neuron types.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation that a short COE motif-containing fragment is not sufficient to drive expression in all unc-3-dependent neurons.

claim: unc-3 activity is required not only for the expression of proper neurotransmitter identity, but also for synaptic connectivity throughout the VNC motor neuron circuit.
source: Taken together, unc-3 activity is required not only for the expression of proper neurotransmitter identity, but also for synaptic connectivity throughout the VNC motor neuron circuit, not just in motor neurons but also in command interneurons.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: unc-3 is not required to control the expression of other identity features of command interneurons, such as the many types of distinct glutamate receptors expressed by the command interneurons.
source: However, as mentioned above, unc-3 is not required to control the expression of other identity features of command interneurons, such as the many types of distinct glutamate receptors expressed by the command interneurons (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The homeobox gene unc-42 is frequently employed in the context of the 'regulated mutual' 3-neuron network motif.
source: On a micro-circuit level, we note that the homeobox gene unc-42 is, like unc-3, also frequently employed in the context of the 'regulated mutual' 3-neuron network motif described above.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of network motifs and unc-42 function.

claim: unc-42 specifies the cholinergic identity of the cross-connected head motor neurons (RMDs, SMDs) and the RIV interneuron that innervates these cross-connected neurons.
source: In the case of the cross-connected head motor neurons (RMDs, SMDs) and the RIV interneuron that innervates these cross-connected neurons, unc-42 specifies the cholinergic identity of all of these neurons (and other signaling input to these neurons, exemplified by the above-mentioned regulation of the metabotropic Glu receptor mgl-1 by unc-42).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: In the cross-connected command interneurons, unc-42 does not affect their cholinergic identity, but it does affect the expression of multiple ionotropic Glu receptors (GluRs) expressed in the command interneurons.
source: In the cross-connected command interneurons, unc-42 does not affect their cholinergic identity, but it does affect the expression of multiple ionotropic Glu receptors (GluRs) expressed in the command interneurons (Brockie et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brockie et al., 2001.

claim: The glutamatergic identity of the ASH neurons is controlled by unc-42.
source: We previously found that the glutamatergic identity of the ASH neurons is controlled by unc-42 (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: unc-42 controls and apparently coordinates the expression of presynaptic neurotransmitter identity and postsynaptic receptor expression in a repulsive reflex circuit.
source: unc-42 therefore controls and apparently coordinates the expression of presynaptic neurotransmitter identity and postsynaptic receptor expression in a repulsive reflex circuit (Figure 9B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 9B and is an inference based on the authors' observations.

claim: Mutually connected, unc-42-dependent head motor neurons are coupled by electrical synapses.
source: Mutually connected, unc-42-dependent head motor neurons are coupled by electrical synapses (Figure 9B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 9B.

claim: The glutamatergic identity of the AIB interneurons is controlled by unc-42.
source: This connection is made by the glutamatergic AIB interneurons; strikingly, their glutamatergic identity is also controlled by unc-42 (E.S. and O.H., unpubl. data).
evidence: This claim is based on unpublished data from the authors.

claim: A network of interconnected neurons in the head of the worm that employ distinct neurotransmitter systems all require unc-42, either for the acquisition of their neurotransmitter identity or for the ability to receive neurotransmitter signals.
source: Taken together, a network of interconnected neurons in the head of the worm that employ distinct neurotransmitter systems all require unc-42, either for the acquisition of their neurotransmitter identity or for the ability to receive neurotransmitter signals (unc-42-dependent GluR expression in command interneurons).
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the authors' experimental observations.
